fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a True and False Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Describe the statements, the pass mark, and who sees the scores. Emergent builds the quiz and the table that holds every answer.
fields.feature_1:
Statements drafted from your notes

Paste a unit outline or a policy page, and Emergent drafts true and false statements from it, about half of them false. A follow-up prompt rewords a statement that gives itself away.
fields.feature_2:
A rewrite box on every false answer

When a taker marks a statement false, the app can ask for a corrected version. You read the rewrites in one list and accept or return each. A lucky tap on False earns no point.
fields.feature_3:
Sure or Guessing beside each answer

Takers mark each of their answers Sure or Guessing. The table lists the wrong answers marked Sure apart from wrong guesses. Reteach what a class believed, not what it guessed.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer saved as a row

Each answer is saved with the taker, the statement, and the confidence mark, in a database you own. Sort by statement to see which one the most takers got wrong, and by whom.
fields.feature_5:
A pass mark that sends an email

Set a pass mark such as 11 of 12, and the app emails a manager or teacher each time a taker lands below it. Emergent puts no cap on responses, for one class or a whole district.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Host the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it next term.

plan.angle: The top 10 for true and false quiz template is static: stock images, Pinterest pins, poster templates, and a Wordwall template that keeps no scores. This page gives the searcher an 8-statement true or false quiz to play on the page, each answer sourced to NASA, NOAA, or the National Park Service, then four builds where the true or false format itself does the work: false answers rewritten, a pass mark on a policy quiz, a live trivia round, and a sure-or-guessing check that separates misconceptions from guesses.
tab_stories: Renata Pasternak's 29 seventh-grade geography students at Halloran Ridge Middle School answer 20 statements, 10 of them false; marking one false opens a box to rewrite it, the point counts once she accepts the rewrite, and of 112 rewrites on Friday she accepted 87 and sent 25 back.

Gilsland Cycle Co. gives each new hire at its 3 shops 12 statements on the returns and repair policy; under 11 of 12 emails service manager Chidi Nkemdirim the statements missed, and this spring 9 of 13 hires passed on the first try.
Calder Flats Taproom ends Thursday trivia with a 15-statement true or false round on phones; 22 teams played, the leaderboard fills in as answers land, and Bitter Enders won with 14 of 15.

Hanne Ruckert's 58 earth science students at Osterbrook Community College mark each of 16 answers Sure or Guessing; 19 marked the atmosphere statement wrong and sure, more than any other, so it opens Tuesday's lecture.
